newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-Lam makes triumphant return to Cardiff.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Lam makes triumphant return to Cardiff.

text.p: CARDIFF, Nov 26 - Pat Lam made a triumphant return to Cardiff as his Western Samoan rugby tourists more than made up for last weekend's lapse at Llanelli by beating Cardiff 53-29, NZPA reported on Wednesday (NZT).
They blew away a shadow Cardiff side at the Arms Park with seven tries as they outgunned the home team.

Lam, the sole survivor from his country's sensational 1991 World Cup win over Wales at the adjacent national ground, led the way from the start as he crossed for his side's opening try after 12 minutes.
First five-eighth Earl Va'a, who had slotted a simple penalty after only three minutes, added the conversion and the tourists were on their way to another stunning victory.
Cardiff were forced to field their second-string team because of international calls and the fact they are still in the Heineken European Cup semifinals.

There will be six Cardiff players in the Welsh lineup against Australia on Sunday, and a seventh on the bench, and the Arms Park Club's coach Terry Holmes obviously didn't want to risk any more of his first teamers against Lam's tough as teak tacklers.
By halftime right wing Pailate Fili and fullback Veli Patu had helped increase the visitors' lead to 22-3. Then it was over to left wing Afato So'oalo to turn on the magic.
The tiny left wing, slippery as an eel to the Cardiff defence, side-stepped his way to a superb second-half hat-trick as the Samoans went on the rampage.
Cardiff opened with a try by young centre Delme Williams four minutes after the restart, but So'oalo's opening try quickly put them back in their place.

Junior Paramore, named as the man of the match, also got his just rewards for a dynamic back row display with a try, although to their credit the young Cardiff side never gave up in the face of much adversity.
They were able to notch four tries in the second-half scoring spree with former New Zealand under-21 cap Lee Jones grabbing one from the Cardiff back row.
But there was no denying the gulf in class, and Samoan coach Bryan Williams will have been more than happy with this triumph at one of the citadels of world rugby.
